principles: Raw payloads are never redistributed. What the site publishes is derived: per-game and per-player tables, the board's values and projections, the schedule with context, aggregates in the notebooks.
The Parquet mirror of the gold tables is served to the site's owner alone (ADR 0008); the JSON the pages read is public.
Betting lines are model inputs and analysis aids: the game line is shown as context, player prop lines are never published (ADR 0008 addendum).

Collection is polite: one request at a time per host with a pacing gap, no retries beyond the shared client's, scheduled runs morning and evening. Outlets' news feeds are read only where their terms allow it, never behind a login, a paywall or a bot check, once per run with a User-Agent that links this page; only the headline, link and date are kept, and the articles are never fetched (ADR 0008 addendum, 2026-11-08). A YouTube channel's captions are fetched from the home connection only, one new video at a time, and never past a bot check or a block; the transcripts are never published (ADR 0008 addendum, 2026-11-08).
The site is free, non-commercial and not affiliated with any of the organisations below. If a source objects, the site complies: open an issue or write to the address on the GitHub profile.

sources.name: NBA.com and WNBA.com statistics
sources.feeds: Game logs, box scores (traditional and advanced), play-by-play, shot charts, player game logs (usage and misc), tracking and hustle, rosters, the player directory, standings and the schedule.
sources.cadence: Daily, with a settling window for late corrections; backfills by season. From a home connection, since the stats host blocks cloud addresses (ADR 0002).
sources.published: Derived per-game and per-player tables, the board's values, projections and rolling lines, shot charts on the player pages, event-level facts in the owner-only Parquet. No raw payload.
sources.retention: Landed payloads are kept on the lakehouse volume (the record of what the API said each day; pruning is written down for 50 GB and has not been needed). Seven published builds are kept.

sources.name: ESPN
sources.feeds: Scoreboard and game summaries (box scores, betting lines), team rosters, injuries, transactions, news headlines, the fantasy market (average draft position and ownership, and each past NBA season's draft positions, landed once for the backtests), player prop lines.
sources.cadence: Daily, morning and evening, from GitHub Actions.
sources.published: Reconciliation against the league box scores, injury status and the expected-return note, schedules with the closing line as context, headline flags and the headline, the market's rank and ownership bucket, the transaction log. Prop lines: never (a private model input).
sources.retention: As above: landed payloads kept, seven published builds.

sources.name: Basketball-Reference
sources.feeds: NBA team payrolls by season (each player's salary), for the contract-year study.
sources.cadence: Once per season: one page per team, at least four seconds apart, from an identified crawler that keeps to robots.txt.
sources.published: Never per player: only the contract-year study's aggregates. Salaries are a private model input.
sources.retention: Landed payloads kept; removed with the source if Sports-Reference objects.

sources.name: Sleeper
sources.feeds: The player directory and the daily waiver trends (adds and drops across Sleeper leagues).
sources.published: The add and drop counts and ranks beside the player, as waiver heat on the Streamers page.

sources.name: The Odds API
sources.feeds: Player prop lines from the bookmakers it aggregates (DraftKings among them).
sources.cadence: Twice daily, behind its key; off until the key is set.
sources.published: Nothing. The lines are a check on the board's projections; the prop-lines notebook publishes aggregates only (ADR 0008 addendum).

sources.name: The leagues' official injury reports
sources.feeds: The official injury report before each game day (the NBA's archive back to 17 December 2018), 5 pm Eastern and the morning's.
sources.cadence: Morning and evening in season; the archive landed once.
sources.published: Each player's official status and reason for the next game, and the calibration of expected games missed built from past listings (aggregates by status and reason).

sources.name: Yahoo Sports
sources.feeds: The NBA and WNBA news RSS feeds: each item's headline, link and publish time. The summary and the articles are never kept or fetched.
sources.cadence: Once each morning and at each evening injury-report run, one request per feed, from an identified client.
sources.published: Nothing. Headlines are an input to the claims the local model reads, which the backtest scores before any of them may tune a number; credited here.
sources.retention: Landed payloads kept on the lakehouse volume; dropped and deleted if Yahoo objects.

sources.name: Hoops Rumors
sources.feeds: The site's RSS feed (NBA): each item's headline, link and publish time. The summary and the articles are never kept or fetched. The site publishes no terms of use; its privacy policy is linked.
sources.retention: Landed payloads kept; dropped and deleted if Hoops Rumors objects.

sources.name: The IX Sports
sources.feeds: The WNBA newsroom's RSS feed: each item's headline, link and publish time. The summary and the articles are never kept or fetched. The site publishes no terms of use; its privacy policy is linked.
sources.retention: Landed payloads kept; dropped and deleted if The IX objects.

sources.name: Winsidr
sources.feeds: The site's RSS feed (WNBA): each item's headline, link and publish time. The summary and the articles are never kept or fetched. The site publishes no terms of use; its robots.txt, which allows the feed, is linked.
sources.retention: Landed payloads kept; dropped and deleted if Winsidr objects.

sources.name: Sporting Logically (YouTube)
sources.feeds: The channel's public video feed (each video's title, description and publish time; no API key) and, from the home connection only, the caption transcripts of its new videos.
sources.cadence: Once a day: one request for the feed, then each new video's captions one at a time, seconds apart, from a client that names this page. The fetch stops at any bot check or block and tries no other way.
sources.published: Nothing. Transcripts stay private: never shown, never exported. Only the claims the local model derives from them are kept, credited to the channel, for the backtest to score.
sources.retention: Landed files kept on the lakehouse volume; dropped and deleted if the channel or YouTube objects.

sources.name: NBA.com referee assignments
sources.published: The crew chief and the crew's tendency (fouls, free throws, pace against average) in the schedule's tooltips and the game context notebook.

retention: Landed payloads stay on the lakehouse volume as the record of what each source said each day; pruning of superseded daily snapshots is written down for when it passes 50 GB and has not been needed.
The published builds the site serves are the newest seven, plus any build a rollback pinned; older ones are deleted after each publish.

A visitor's watchlist, theme and league choice live in their own browser and nowhere else. The league setup does too, unless the visitor signs in with Yahoo to save it: then the setup is stored on the server under an account id derived from the Yahoo id (never the Yahoo id itself), and "Delete my saved data" on the League page removes it. Sign-ins keep a signed cookie and no token.

The data holds no personal information beyond what the sources publish about public athletes, coaches and officials; a request to remove a source, or a person's rows, goes through the repository's issues and the runbook's procedure.
